title: GPT-6 Astra Minor: OpenAI Demoted the Sun, Now the Star Gets a Mini
description: Astra Minor is one vanished line in an Azure file, Sol slid from flagship to middle tier, and Opus 5.5 now beats Astra on most of Anthropic's table at 40% of the price
imageAlt: Notebook sketch of GPT-6 Astra Minor with a demoted Sol, a missing Terra and the $10 / $50 Astra price
body:
## 3-Line TL;DR

- GPT-6 Astra Minor is one unannounced name from an Azure config file, with no price, spec or date, and it was gone from that file when I checked on September 28
- The naming is the real story: Sol went from GPT-5.6 flagship to GPT-6 middle tier, and Terra disappeared while Sol took over its "balance intelligence and cost" line
- Opus 5.5 beat Astra on three of five scored rows in Anthropic's own table at 40% of the price, so OpenAI needs a real answer, and DevDay on September 29 is the next place to look

## Astra Minor is one line in an Azure file

- On September 22, a user on the Chinese developer forum locdd.com spotted three unannounced OpenAI registry paths in Azure's public playground config ([OrcaRouter](https://www.orcarouter.ai/blog/gpt-6-astra-minor-leak))
- They were `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna` and `gpt-6-astra-minor`
- Sol and Luna are now live products on OpenAI's API ([OpenAI models](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models))
- Astra Minor has no price, context window, benchmark or announcement
- Neither Microsoft nor OpenAI has confirmed it
- I opened the same Azure file on September 28, and it listed `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6-luna`, with no `astra-minor`
- A missing line can mean a cancelled model, a renamed one, or just a cleaned-up config file

## Sol went from flagship to the middle seat

![GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, Luna next to GPT-6 Astra, Sol, Luna, with Sol moved from top to middle and Astra Minor as a dashed slot](/images/posts/ai/gpt-6-astra-minor-naming-ladder.webp)

*Sources: [OpenAI models](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) and [OpenAI pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), standard short-context rates checked September 28, 2026 — diagram by HSL*

| Tier | GPT-5.6 | GPT-6 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Top | Sol, "flagship," $4 / $20 | Astra, "most capable," $10 / $50 |
| Middle | Terra, $2 / $12 | Sol, $2 / $10 |
| Low | Luna, $0.20 / $1.20 | Luna, $0.10 / $0.50 |

- GPT-5.6 had a tidy sun, earth and moon lineup
- OpenAI's docs called GPT-5.6 Sol the "flagship model for complex professional work" ([OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol))
- GPT-5.6 Terra was "designed for workloads that balance intelligence and cost" ([OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-terra))
- In GPT-6, OpenAI's own guidance says to "choose GPT-6 Sol to balance intelligence and cost"
- So Terra's job description survived, and Terra did not
- The sun now sits under a star, and the star may be getting a smaller version of itself
- My take: keeping Sol, Terra and Luna and adding Astra on top would have told buyers more than "Astra Minor" does
- GPT-6 Sol does cost less than GPT-5.6 Sol: $2 / $10 against $4 / $20
- It is the same $2 / $10 Anthropic charges for Sonnet 5 ([Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview))
- Between Astra and GPT-6 Sol, the list price jumps five times on both input and output
- A model in that gap would make commercial sense, but that is my inference, not something OpenAI has said

## Opus 5.5 took Astra's lead within three weeks

![Bar chart of five benchmarks: Opus 5.5 leads Humanity's Last Exam, Terminal-Bench 4.0 and FrontierCode; Astra leads two rows](/images/posts/ai/gpt-6-astra-minor-opus-vs-astra.webp)

*Source: [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5) — Claude Opus 5.5 benchmark table, vendor-reported — chart by HSL*

- Astra launched September 3, and Opus 5.5 followed on September 22
- On Anthropic's table, Opus 5.5 leads Humanity's Last Exam by 10.5 points and Terminal-Bench 4.0 by 8.5
- FrontierCode is nearly a tie, 54.4% to 53.3%
- Astra keeps AutomationBench by 1.4 points and Terminal-Bench-Science by 5.9
- Opus also leads GDPval-AA v2.1, 1846 to 1542
- Anthropic chose the benchmarks and ran its own side, so this is a vendor report card, not a neutral test
- The price gap is not close: Astra lists at $10 / $50, Opus at $4 / $20
- OpenAI's newest top model now costs 2.5 times a rival that beats it on most of that table
- In one same-prompt game test, Opus still ran up a bigger bill on one of two rounds, as the [Astra vs Opus 5.5 test](/en/posts/gpt-6-sol-luna-opus-5-5-cost-per-success/) showed

## OpenAI gets a stage on September 29, with no 6.1 on the list

- My view is that OpenAI needs a GPT-6.1 soon, not another tier name
- I found no credible GPT-6.1 report, only this Astra Minor leak
- OpenAI DevDay is Tuesday, September 29, at Fort Mason in San Francisco, with a 10 a.m. keynote by Sam Altman ([DevDay](https://devday.openai.com/))
- The event page promises "a closer look at what OpenAI teams are building," and names no model
- Anthropic has also said Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 will follow "in the coming weeks" ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5))
- A Sonnet 5.5 would land in the same $2 / $10 slot as GPT-6 Sol if its price follows Sonnet 5

| Your situation | What I would do |
| :--- | :--- |
| Using Astra for hard back-end or science work | Keep it, since Astra still leads the automation and science rows |
| Paying Astra rates for routine coding | Test Opus 5.5 on the same tasks and compare cost per finished task |
| Waiting for Astra Minor to save money | Try GPT-6 Sol now, because Astra Minor has no price or date |
| Still on GPT-5.6 Sol | Check GPT-6 Sol first, which lists at half the price |

## Q&A (Field Notes)

- **Q. Can I call Astra Minor through the API?**
  - No, it is not in OpenAI's model list, and the Azure entry was gone when I checked on September 28
- **Q. Is GPT-6 Sol the successor to GPT-5.6 Sol?**
  - By name yes, by role no, since GPT-6 Sol is now the middle tier under Astra
- **Q. What happened to Terra?**
  - GPT-6 has no Terra, and OpenAI's catalog now describes Sol with Terra's old "balance intelligence and cost" line
- **Q. Is GPT-6.1 coming at DevDay?**
  - Nothing says so, and the event page names no model
